messages:
ashley (arch): Thinking out loud — proposal to add a lightweight "residency escrow" token that proxies attach when they prove a tenant's region consent. purpose: allow active/active failover without leaking residency-violating replicas.

mike (infra): curious — how small are we talking? signed JWT-ish? or a header blob persisted in the routing plane?

ashley (arch): signed token (short expiry, ~30s) with region=true/false, consent_ts, and node_id. idea: routers cache token TTL and honor it during circuit-breaker failover. not a permanent record, just operational proof.

leila (privacy): must include consent scope (e.g., "pii_needs_eu") and audience so it can't be reused outside the residency boundary. also audit log entry when token is generated.

ashley (arch): agreed. sample header we sketched:

```
X-Residency-Escrow: region=eu;scope=pii_needs_eu;exp=1680000123;sig=BASE64
```

cyra (sre): operational question — when failover happens, do we block requests that lack escrow or do we downgrade to a non-PII-safe model variant? both have tradeoffs.

mike (infra): propose flow: 1) Router receives request; 2) if tenant has residency flag, require escrow; 3) if escrow missing, try local region; 4) if local unavailable and escrow present, continue; 5) if local unavailable and escrow missing, return 451 or signal fallback-mode based on tenant policy. keep it explicit per-tenant.

leila (privacy): we can add an opt-in fallback policy per tenant: "strict" (fail hard), "graceful" (mask PII + route), "consent-request" (ask client for explicit consent). default to strict for enterprise.

ashley (arch): question for infra: can the router generate an escrow for requests that originate from the tenant's control-plane (i.e., console actions) so admin flows still work during partial outage?

mike (infra): yes, control-plane nodes can mint escrows with a different key and shorter TTL. need KMS scoping and separate logs.

cyra (sre): cache handoff concerns: if we failover active->active, KV caches may contain sensitive prefixes. should we evict or tag entries with residency stamps so they can't be served cross-region?

ashley (arch): tag-by-stamp seems best: every cache entry gets residency_stamp = token.signature_id and region label. router enforces serving only if token matches or entry is global-safe. eviction is heavier and causes cold start.

mike (infra): implementation note: we can embed the stamp in cache key: `tenant:resid:stamp:...`. stamp rotation on lease-swap needs to be near-atomic. maybe use lease epochs.

leila (privacy): audit: when stamp changes, emit an event with old_stamp -> new_stamp and tenant_id. this helps prove we didn't serve data outside scope.

cyra (sre): rollout plan? start with read-only proof-of-concept in staging for a subset of EU tenants, test failover simulation, then gate on audit outputs.

ashley (arch): timeline suggestion: week 1: prototype escrow header + minting service; week 2: router honor/deny logic + stamp-key changes; week 3: staging failover tests + privacy audit.

mike (infra): I'll spin up a minimal mint service and add a feature flag in the router. deploy-bot: canary when ready?

deploy-bot: canary pipeline queued for infra/escrow-proto, expected deploy in ~2h :package:
